items.User: create a perfect  replica of spss make it light weight and seemless

Step.text: Clean room: nothing inside it is read…

Agent.text: I'm checking whether the Rust build tools are installed on this computer before building.
Rust is set up inside the project. Now recording what we know and planning the build.

Plan.text: Make the data sheet and the variable list
Add the menus for data, transforms and analyses
Show results as tables and charts in an output window
Build it, take a picture and check it

Agent.text: Rust is ready. Now writing the app itself: the data sheet, variable list, analysis menus, output window and charts.
Setting up one more piece the Windows build needs (a small linker helper), then I'll keep writing the app.
The computer's disk just ran out of space. Checking how much room is left.
The disk is full, so the tools can't run. The build files I made inside the app folder are using space, so I'll try deleting them.

request.title: Allow: Run a build command
request.detail: Run a build command runs code or changes a device, so it needs your OK first.

Agent.text: There's about 2.5 GB free again. I'll make the build use much less disk space and continue.
Now re-saving the output and chart code that the full disk interrupted.
Writing the statistics engine next (descriptives, frequencies, crosstabs, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation, regression, reliability, non-parametric tests and chart data).
The build needs one more fix (a helper program it expects isn't included). I'll pin a few library versions to avoid it. First, re-saving the statistics code, which didn't save.
Now checking which libraries need the missing helper.
Fixed: no library needs the missing helper now. Building the libraries in the background while I write the rest.
Now the analysis dialog boxes (the variable pickers with OK / Paste / Reset / Cancel / Help).
One more library needs the same missing helper. Checking which libraries in the project still depend on it.
Only one library left. Pinning it to an older version that doesn't need the helper.
While the libraries build, writing the main window: menus, toolbar, file handling and the command runner.
Libraries built. Now the last big piece: the data sheet, variable list, output viewer, syntax editor and toolbar icons.
It compiled. Only one small Windows system library file is missing when joining the pieces together. I'll make a stand-in for it from a file the libraries already include.
The app builds. Taking a test picture of it now.
Distribution maths checks out. Now running analyses on the sample data and photographing the output window.
The output window works: outline on the left, results with their command log, tables and a bar chart. Checking the t-test and regression tables too.
Tables match the classic statistics-package layout (titles, grouped headers, footnotes). Now running the official check.

Step.text: The builder is checking its work against the original…
The builder checked its work: 0 of 1 checks pass.

Agent.text: The official check can't find the Rust build tools, because I installed them inside the project rather than system-wide. Checking whether Craft Anything has a setting that points it to them.
Both the dialog and the Variable View look right. Next I'll run every remaining procedure in one go to make sure none of them crash or report errors.
All 20 commands ran. Only the deliberately wrong command showed an error message, as expected. Checking how the charts look.
The charts look right too. Now making the optimized, small release version of the app.
